champion: Cerebral Vasculitis associated with Systemic Sclerosis
ordered_diagnoses: Cerebral Vasculitis associated with Systemic Sclerosis

facts.raw_span: A 41-year-old woman with a 3-year history of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis
skin sclerosis of the fingers, hands, forearms, and face
Raynaud’s phenomenon with digital ulcers
multiple facial telangiectasias
esophageal reflux
interstitial lung disease
nail-fold capillaroscopy showed capillary loss with dilatation and microhemorrhages
a forearm skin biopsy demonstrated increased dermal collagen and superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltration
positive antinuclear antibody titer (>1:320) with a nucleolar pattern
cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed protein 161.6 mg/dL, glucose 39 mg/dL, red blood cells 0 /mm3, and white blood cells 459 /mm3
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated T2 hyperintense lesions in the frontal, left parietal, and left occipital lobes with leptomeningeal enhancement
emergent cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries and their branches
